title: Supreme Court judgment — Harpreet Singh Talwar @ Kabir Talwar vs The State Of Gujarat
text: The prosecution case recorded by the Court alleges that Harpreet Singh Talwar played a central and coordinating role in facilitating a consignment of heroin-laced talc stones imported into India through Mundra Port under the cover of M/s Magent India. The judgment states that 2,988.21 kg of heroin was seized at Mundra, allegedly originating from Afghanistan and routed through Bandar Abbas, Iran, in a consignment addressed to M/s Aashi Trading Company. It further records allegations that Talwar met Vityash Koser @ Raju Dubai in Dubai, after introduction through Sunny Kakkar; that Talwar instructed his accountant Sunil Jain to arrange registration of M/s Magent India in the name of employee Prince Sharma; and that Amit Sharma, described as a known associate of Raju Dubai, visited Talwar's office and obtained import documents. The judgment also states that Talwar was later named as Accused No. 24 in a supplementary charge-sheet.

title: Indian Express report on NIA arrest of Sobhan Aryanfar
text: The NIA arrested Afghan national Sobhan Aryanfar in the Mundra port drug haul case. The report says the case involved seizure of 2,988.21 kg heroin at Gujarat's Mundra Port. The heroin was found in two containers declared as semi-processed talc stones that arrived from Afghanistan via Iran's Bandar Abbas Port in the name of Aashi Trading Company of Vijayawada. The report identifies Machavaram Sudhakar, Durga PV Govindaraju and Rajkumar P among accused named in the FIR. It says Sudhakar and Govindaraju were associated with Aashi Trading Company and Rajkumar worked in Iran and was allegedly coordinating with foreign suppliers.

title: Gujarat High Court order concerning Harpreet Singh Talwar
text: Court material records the prosecution theory that Talwar opened or controlled multiple firms through friends, employees and known persons, with documents and trade allegedly controlled through an accountant and close aides. It states that Talwar directed his accountant Sunil Jain to open M/s Magent India in the name of Prince Sharma, and that M/s Jesus Christ Impex was used in the described movement of an earlier heroin-laden consignment toward Delhi.

title: Gujarat High Court order concerning Rajkumar Perumal
text: The prosecution account states that the 2,988.21 kg narcotics shipment was sent from Afghanistan to Mundra in the guise of semi-processed talc stones. The order describes Rajkumar as a middleman for Aashi Trading Company, allegedly facilitating an Afghan supplier by IEC, customs clearance and logistics support. It also states that the arrangements for customs clearance and transportation from Mundra to Alipur were organized pursuant to directions attributed to Afghan national Mohammad Hussain Dad.
